verses.text: One day Ruth's mother-in-law Naomi said to her, "My daughter, I must find a home for you, where you will be well cared for.
Boaz, whose women you have been working with, is our relative. Tonight he will be separating the barley from the chaff on the threshing floor.
So wash, put on perfume, and get dressed in your best clothes. Then go down to the threshing floor, but do not let him know you are there until he has finished eating and drinking.
When he lies down, notice the place where he is lying. Then go and uncover his feet and lie down. He will tell you what to do."
"I will do whatever you say," Ruth answered.
So she went down to the threshing floor and did everything her mother-in-law told her to do.
When Boaz had finished eating and drinking and was in a good mood, he went to lie down at the far end of the pile of grain. Ruth went over quietly, uncovered his feet and lay down.
In the middle of the night something startled the man. He turned over, and there was a woman lying at his feet!
"Who are you?" he asked. "I am your servant Ruth," she said. "Spread the corner of your garment over me, because you are a family protector who can redeem me."
"The LORD bless you, my daughter," he replied. "This kindness is even greater than what you showed earlier. You have not run after the younger men, whether rich or poor.
And now, my daughter, do not be afraid. I will do for you all you ask. All the people of my town know that you are a woman of fine character.
It is true that I am a family protector who can redeem you, but there is another man who is a closer relative than I.

Stay here tonight. In the morning, if he wants to do his duty as your family protector, good. Let him redeem you. But if he is not willing, as surely as the LORD lives, I will do it. Lie here until morning."
So she lay at his feet until morning, but she got up before anyone could be recognised. He said, "No one must know that a woman came to the threshing floor."
He also said, "Bring me the shawl you are wearing and hold it out." When she did so, he poured six measures of barley into it and put it on her. Then he went back to town.
When Ruth came to her mother-in-law, Naomi asked, "How did it go, my daughter?" Then she told her everything Boaz had done for her
and added, "He gave me these six measures of barley, saying, 'Do not go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed.'"
Then Naomi said, "Wait, my daughter, until you find out what happens. The man will not rest until the matter is settled today."
